name: rust-multitarget-crate-identity
body:
The Rust frontend scans a Cargo package that declares both a library target and a binary target, giving each crate a distinct, stable module identity, so `apg scan` completes free of a duplicate-FQN panic and the two crates' units are addressable under separate module prefixes.

`rust.apg-rustfrontend.package_prefix_map` assigns the cargo package name as a module prefix when the package has exactly one local crate target and assigns per-target prefixes when the package has multiple crate targets; `rust.apg-rustfrontend.crate_prefix` uses each target's prefix. When the lib and bin targets share a name (the default, e.g. `[package] name = "apg"`), the two crate roots render distinct module FQNs rather than sharing `rust.apg` and tripping `rust.apg.ingest.insert_node` on a duplicate project node FQN.

Acceptance criteria:
- `apg scan` of a package with both a library and a binary target completes free of a duplicate-FQN panic.
- The two crate roots render distinct module FQNs.
- Each crate's units are reachable under its own module prefix (module-based tools enumerate both subtrees).
- Every package that scans keeps its FQNs (see `requirements.constraint.rust-crate-fqn-stability`).
